summary:
ANOS is an AI-powered fire safety dashboard built on real NASA microgravity combustion data. It addresses the core challenge by transforming three decades of ISS experimental results, spread across dozens of files and publications, into one queryable system that answers direct spacecraft fire safety questions.

A mission engineer selects a material, oxygen concentration, and airflow direction. The system finds the most relevant NASA experiments, ranks them by condition similarity, and returns a grounded risk assessment with every figure traceable to a verified NASA PSI source.

The data backbone covers three real ISS investigations. BASS-II tested solid polymer and fabric flammability across 129 controlled conditions. FLEX-2 documented cool-flame extinction in liquid fuel droplets across pressures from 0.5 to 3 atm. SAFFIRE-I burned a full-scale 94 cm fabric sample inside a Cygnus spacecraft, revealing that ventilation direction alone produces a 6x difference in burn duration.

This matters because Artemis and Mars missions cannot rely on Earth-based fire standards. Our system makes the gap between lab tests and mission reality visible, actionable, and grounded in the best data NASA has ever collected on fire in space.
details:
ANOS is an AI-powered dashboard that answers one question no existing tool can. Given a specific spacecraft material, oxygen level, and airflow configuration, what does NASA’s own experimental data say about fire risk?

The system ingests real microgravity combustion data from three NASA ISS experiments — BASS-II (solid material flame spread, PSI-25), FLEX-2 (liquid fuel cool-flame extinction, PSI-68), and SAFFIRE-I (large-scale spacecraft fire, PSI-98) — and surfaces the most relevant findings for any mission scenario a user defines.

When an engineer asks “Can I use SIBAL fabric at 21.5% O₂ with concurrent airflow?”, the dashboard retrieves the matching experiments, ranks them by condition proximity, and returns a grounded answer with burn duration, thermal peak, smoke onset, and a risk score. Every figure is traceable to a NASA DOI. No hallucination is possible because every output is sourced directly from PSI raw telemetry files and peer-reviewed publications.

What makes it different. Prior to SAFFIRE (2016), spacecraft fire safety was extrapolated from small 7 cm lab samples. Our system makes the scale gap visible. The same SIBAL fabric burns 420 seconds in concurrent flow versus 70 seconds opposed, a 6x difference driven purely by ventilation direction. That insight, buried across three separate NASA investigations, is surfaced in one interaction.

Stack. NASA PSI data (CSV, XLSX, TXT telemetry), Python for data extraction and enrichment, Power BI for the interactive dashboard, grounded on three DOI-verified sources (PSI-25, PSI-68, PSI-98).

Impact. Directly applicable to Artemis lunar habitat design and future Mars missions, where a fire is not survivable and material selection decisions are made years before launch.
